data.why: The repo ships all results and demo assets the app reads (results/audit_table.csv, results/oof_predictions.parquet, results/enrichment.csv and other optional results/*, demo/assets/compounds.parquet, demo/assets/dose_response.parquet, demo/assets/images/* and demo/assets/cell_lines/* with their manifests), so no data needs to be copied or synthesized.

goals: For a given toxicology endpoint, see whether the full Cell Painting morphology model has a certified advantage over a cell-count-only baseline after multiple-testing correction
Check how well the model's predicted probabilities are calibrated (reliability diagram, Brier score, ECE) for a chosen endpoint
Look up a specific compound and compare its measured activity against morphology-model and cell-count-model predictions across endpoints
Find out whether the morphology advantage is concentrated in particular assay or target families via enrichment testing
See example Cell Painting images (treated vs DMSO) and compare cell lines to build intuition for what morphology features capture
Plan sample size and design choices (baseline, grouping, endpoints) for a smaller organ-on-chip study using the audit's simulation results

review.summary: The tree captures what the tool is for: certifying, one endpoint at a time, whether morphology beats a strong cell-count baseline, then planning an organ-on-chip study. Its phases, tasks and features are well cut and backed by the 8 screens I checked. Before filing it needs the missing HepG2 second-source comparison, the robustness check as a task of its own, and a corrected note on the CSV export.
